chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, who said:

I saw Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) sitting with one of his legs placed on his thigh. I said: 'The people dislike this sitting posture and say: It is the sitting of the Lord.' He said: 'I only sat in this posture for tiredness, and the Lord does not get tired, nor does slumber seize Him, nor sleep.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the sitting posture of placing one leg on the thigh in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) refutes the superstition that this posture is exclusive to God by attributing it to human fatigue (malal), thereby distinguishing created limitations from divine perfection. This narration is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for validating the 'sitting of the Prophet' (tawarruk) and other common postures against claims of shirk or divine imitation. It underscores the principle that physical comfort does not imply ontological divinity, a key concept in understanding Islamic etiquette (adab).
